html:
The Football Association rules were the common laws of football agreed by a group of London clubs and schools, who founded the Football Association in a London pub in October 1863. They are the start of association football, or soccer, now the most popular sport in the world.

Football games had been played in Britain for centuries, often rough contests between whole villages. In the 1800s the public schools each played their own version, some allowing players to carry the ball. When former pupils wanted to play each other, they needed shared rules.

At the Freemasons' Tavern in London, a few clubs and schools met to agree them over several meetings. The big quarrel was over hacking (kicking opponents' shins) and carrying the ball. The majority banned both, and the clubs that wanted them left; their game grew into rugby football, which formed its own union in 1871.

What followed:

  • The FA Cup, the oldest football competition, began in 1871.
  • The first international match, Scotland against England, was played in 1872.
  • Professional players were allowed in 1885, and the Football League began in 1888.

British sailors, workers, engineers and teachers carried the game to Europe, South America and around the world, much as Victorian Britain carried its trade. FIFA, the world governing body, was founded in Paris in 1904, and the first World Cup was played in Uruguay in 1930. Other codes grew from the same roots, including Australian rules football and American football.
